changes: No substantive changes: Haripatideva as scribe (coyā = 'wrote', not the causative coyakā), the NS 801 date and the CE 1681 conversion are all correct

Notes expanded: '(2)?' may be the cataloguer's line marker rather than an alternative last digit; the -deva ending is taken as part of the name; the mantra after the colophon names no copy-related persons

notes: 'samvat' with no named era, in a Newari colophon (coyā juro), is read as Nepāla Saṃvat: NS 801 = c. 1681 CE. The '(2)?' after 801 may be the cataloguer's line-number marker, or it may mark a doubtful last digit (802 = c. 1682 CE). The catalogue gives 801. 'Haripatidevana' is the ergative ('by Haripatideva'). The -deva ending is kept as part of the name, but no king of this name is known, so it is not treated as a regnal name. 'coyā juro' means 'was written', so the role is scribe, not commissioner. After the colophon comes a vernacular (Hindi/Bhojpuri-coloured) mantra invoking Kāmākhyā Devī of Kāmarūpa (kāmarideśa kaṃmacchādevi), with a jogī and a list of gifts. It names no persons connected with the copy.
